description: Per-skill capability evals ported from the 2026-04 skill-evals audit (originally .agents/skills/*/evals/evals.json, which nothing executed). Routing, auth/ETL, GFQL, visualization, AI, connectors, REST. The original assertions are semantic, so they are graded by oracle rubric and forbidden_concepts; deterministic checks only anchor explicit code/API tokens. RUN WITH --grading hybrid (or oracle): under deterministic-only grading the semantic assertions are not evaluated.

cases.prompt: How do I get a JWT token from Graphistry Hub using my username and password via the REST API?

rubric: Shows POST to /api/v2/ auth endpoint
Returns a JWT/Bearer token
Uses env vars for username/password, not hardcoded literals
oracle.reference_answer: Shows POST /api/v2/o/token/ (or equivalent auth endpoint) with username/password body, returns token to use as Bearer in subsequent requests

cases.prompt: What's the REST API call to upload a graph (edges CSV) to Graphistry Hub and get back a shareable graph URL?

rubric: Shows upload endpoint /api/v2/upload/ or equivalent
Uses Bearer token auth header
Explains how to construct or retrieve the shareable graph.html URL
oracle.reference_answer: Shows POST to /api/v2/upload/edges/ or dataset endpoint with Bearer auth, explains how to get the graph URL from the response

cases.prompt: I'm embedding a Graphistry graph in an iframe. What URL parameters can I use to disable the toolbar and set the initial zoom level?

rubric: Names a real parameter that hides the toolbar/menu (e.g. menu=false, info=false), either as a graph.html query param or via settings(url_params=...)
Explains the initial view correctly: there is no single zoom parameter; the camera is set via bounds (left/right/top/bottom)
oracle.reference_answer: Either graph.html?dataset=<id>&menu=false&info=false or g.settings(url_params={'menu': False, 'info': False}). Initial view is set with left/right/top/bottom bounds, not a zoom scalar.

cases.prompt: How do I use the PyGraphistry Python library to register with Graphistry and call .plot() on my DataFrame?

rubric: Answers with the PyGraphistry Python SDK path: graphistry.register(api=3) then .edges(...).plot()
Does not answer a Python SDK question with raw REST/curl calls
oracle.reference_answer: Uses the PyGraphistry Python SDK: graphistry.register(api=3, ...) then g.edges(df, 'src', 'dst').plot(). Not raw REST/curl.
forbidden_concepts: Does not answer with curl or raw /api/v2/ endpoint calls for the Python SDK question

cases.prompt: I have an edges CSV with src and dst columns. How do I load it into Graphistry and get an interactive graph?

rubric: Gives the pygraphistry load-and-plot workflow (register, edges binding, plot)
Shows graphistry.register() with api=3
Uses environment variables for credentials, not hardcoded values
oracle.reference_answer: Shows graphistry.register(api=3) plus graphistry.edges(df,'src','dst').plot(), with credentials read from environment variables.

cases.prompt: What's the curl command to upload a graph to Graphistry Hub and get back a shareable URL?

rubric: Gives the REST upload workflow rather than the Python SDK
References /api/v2/ upload endpoint
Shows Bearer token auth pattern
oracle.reference_answer: Shows the /api/v2/upload/ endpoint with Bearer token auth, returning a shareable URL.

cases.prompt: I want to both query my graph with Cypher AND share the result as a link. Which graphistry tools do I need?

rubric: Identifies pygraphistry-gfql for Cypher query
Identifies pygraphistry-visualization for sharing
oracle.reference_answer: Covers both halves: a GFQL/Cypher query for the traversal, and a shareable link (privacy-aware) for the result.

cases.prompt: I'm building a networkx graph and want to run Louvain community detection. How do I do that?

rubric: Answers with networkx or python-louvain community_louvain
oracle.reference_answer: Answers with networkx / python-louvain community detection directly; no Graphistry component is needed for Louvain.
forbidden_concepts: Does not call graphistry.register() or graphistry.edges()

cases.prompt: I have a graph with node feature columns (transaction_count, avg_amount, days_active). How do I run UMAP to find clusters and visualize them in Graphistry?

rubric: Runs UMAP over the node feature columns via g.umap(...)
Accepts either g.umap(X=[...]) directly (umap auto-featurizes) or an explicit g.featurize(...).umap()
Plots or visualizes the resulting clusters
oracle.reference_answer: g.umap(X=['transaction_count','avg_amount','days_active']).plot(); umap() auto-featurizes when given column names, so a separate featurize() call is optional.

cases.prompt: After running UMAP on my graph, how do I identify and label the outlier nodes as anomalies using DBSCAN?

rubric: Uses .dbscan() after umap()
Explains cluster label -1 as outlier/anomaly
oracle.reference_answer: Shows g.dbscan() or g.umap().dbscan() chaining, explains cluster=-1 as anomaly label, shows how to filter and highlight anomalous nodes

cases.prompt: I want to do semantic search over my graph nodes - find nodes similar to a given text query using embeddings. How?

rubric: Uses a real semantic-search entry point: g.search(...) / g.search_graph(...) for a text query, or g.embed(...) when building embeddings
Explains that the text query is matched against node embeddings/features
oracle.reference_answer: g.search('query text') or g.search_graph('query text') for text-to-node semantic search; g.embed() builds the embedding model.

cases.prompt: I want to run the Louvain community detection algorithm on my graph without using Graphistry. Just pure networkx.

rubric: Runs Louvain with networkx itself (nx.algorithms.community.louvain_communities) or python-louvain (community_louvain.best_partition)
Does not route the answer through Graphistry, which the prompt excluded
oracle.reference_answer: networkx>=3.0 ships Louvain natively: from networkx.algorithms.community import louvain_communities; louvain_communities(G). python-louvain's community_louvain.best_partition(G) is an equally valid alternative.
forbidden_concepts: Does not import graphistry or call graphistry.register()

cases.prompt: How do I load a Neo4j graph into PyGraphistry for visualization? I have nodes and relationships I want to explore.

rubric: Uses the real Neo4j path: graphistry.register(..., bolt={...}) then graphistry.cypher('MATCH ...')
Or binds a manually-fetched nodes/edges DataFrame with .edges(...).nodes(...)
Keeps Neo4j credentials in environment variables
oracle.reference_answer: graphistry.register(api=3, bolt={'uri':..., 'auth':...}) then graphistry.cypher('MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) RETURN a,r,b'). There is no from_neo4j() method.

cases.prompt: I'm querying Splunk for network connection events and want to visualize the src/dest IP pairs as a graph in Graphistry. How?

rubric: Shows path from Splunk query result to graphistry.edges()
References Splunk SDK, splunklib, or DataFrame ingest approach
oracle.reference_answer: Shows Splunk connector or DataFrame ingest path: run SPL query -> load into DataFrame -> graphistry.edges(df, 'src_ip', 'dest_ip').plot()

cases.prompt: How do I connect PyGraphistry to a Databricks table and build a graph from a SQL query?

rubric: Shows Databricks or Spark DataFrame -> graphistry binding path
Uses env vars for Databricks credentials
oracle.reference_answer: Shows Databricks connector or spark/JDBC approach to read a table into a DataFrame, then bind edges/nodes in PyGraphistry

cases.prompt: I already have my data in a pandas DataFrame with src and dst columns. I just want to make a quick graph - no external DB.

rubric: Gives the direct DataFrame path (graphistry.edges(...).plot()) with no connector detour
oracle.reference_answer: Shows the direct path: graphistry.edges(df,'src','dst').plot(). No connector is needed for an in-memory DataFrame.
forbidden_concepts: Does not suggest a connector or external data source integration

cases.prompt: I just installed pygraphistry. How do I authenticate against Graphistry Hub and plot my first graph from two DataFrames?

rubric: Uses graphistry.register(api=3, ...)
Reads credentials from os.environ or os.getenv, not hardcoded
Calls .plot()
oracle.reference_answer: Shows graphistry.register(api=3, username=os.environ[...], password=os.environ[...]), .edges()/.nodes() binding, and .plot(). Uses env vars for credentials.
forbidden_concepts: Does not hardcode username or password literals

cases.prompt: I have a wide event log table with columns actor, target, event_type, timestamp. How do I build a hypergraph from it?

rubric: Uses graphistry.hypergraph()
Accesses hg['graph'].plot() or equivalent
oracle.reference_answer: Shows graphistry.hypergraph(df, ['actor', 'target', 'event_type']) and hg['graph'].plot()

cases.prompt: My edges DataFrame has null values in the src column and the plot looks wrong. How do I diagnose and fix this?

rubric: Addresses null handling in src/dst columns
Mentions materialize_nodes() or node binding
oracle.reference_answer: Shows null-check/drop pattern on src/dst columns, suggests materialize_nodes() if node list is missing, confirms column type consistency

cases.prompt: I have a working plot and now want to color nodes by their 'risk_score' column and add badges showing the severity label. How?

rubric: Shows encode_point_color for the risk_score column
Covers badge/icon encoding for the severity indicator
oracle.reference_answer: Shows encode_point_color for the risk_score column and encode_point_badge / encode_point_icon for the severity indicator.

cases.prompt: I want to find all accounts that are within 3 hops of any flagged fraud node in my transaction graph. Show me the GFQL chain-list syntax.

rubric: Gives a GFQL chain-list bounded to 3 hops from the flagged fraud nodes
Uses an edge matcher (e_forward / e_undirected / e_reverse) with min_hops/max_hops or hops
Seeds on the flagged-fraud node predicate
oracle.reference_answer: g.gfql([n({'fraud_flag': True}), e_undirected(min_hops=1, max_hops=3), n()]) -- e_forward is equally valid; output_min_hops/output_max_hops are real optional params.
forbidden_concepts: Does not use deprecated hop() or chain() methods

cases.prompt: Can I write a Cypher query to find people who know someone over 30 years old in my PyGraphistry graph?

rubric: Uses g.gfql() with a Cypher string argument
Shows WHERE clause with property filter
Mentions label__Person column mapping or recommends WHERE p.type='Person' as simpler alternative
oracle.reference_answer: Shows g.gfql("MATCH (p:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(q) WHERE q.age > 30 RETURN p.name") or equivalent. Explains label__Person column mapping if needed.

cases.prompt: How do I use Let bindings in GFQL to define reusable subgraph patterns as named variables?

rubric: Shows Let binding or DAG variable syntax in GFQL
Includes a concrete example with named pattern variable
oracle.reference_answer: Shows Let/DAG binding syntax with named pattern variables, explains scoping rules, gives a concrete example

cases.prompt: How do I change the color of nodes in my PyGraphistry plot based on a 'category' column?

rubric: Shows encode_point_color keyed on the 'category' column
Uses a categorical mapping rather than a continuous/gradient encoding
oracle.reference_answer: Shows encode_point_color keyed on the 'category' column using a categorical mapping.
forbidden_concepts: Does not answer the styling question with GFQL syntax

cases.prompt: I have a working PyGraphistry plot. How do I color nodes by a 'category' column and size them by their 'degree' column?

rubric: Uses encode_point_color() with categorical_mapping
Uses encode_point_size() or bind(point_size=...)
oracle.reference_answer: Shows .encode_point_color('category', categorical_mapping={...}) and .encode_point_size('degree') with a concrete example

cases.prompt: How do I export my PyGraphistry graph as a static PNG image for a report?

rubric: Names a real static-export mechanism: g.plot_static(format='png', path=...)
Does not invent a non-existent export API
oracle.reference_answer: g.plot_static(format='png', path='out.png') renders a static image via the graphviz engine; returns bytes/display object.

cases.prompt: I want to share a Graphistry graph link with a client but only allow viewing, not editing or downloading the data. How do I set that up?

rubric: References privacy mode or private sharing
Shows how to generate a view-only shareable URL
oracle.reference_answer: Shows privacy mode settings, sharing URL controls, token-safe link generation with privacy: 'private' or url_params for view-only access
forbidden_concepts: Does not put JWT or credentials in a URL query parameter

cases.prompt: I want to find all nodes within 2 hops of a fraud node in my graph. What GFQL pattern should I use?

rubric: Gives a GFQL traversal for 2 hops from the fraud node
Uses g.gfql() with a chain-list or Cypher pattern bounded to 2 hops
oracle.reference_answer: Shows a GFQL 2-hop traversal from the fraud node via g.gfql(), using a chain-list or Cypher pattern.
forbidden_concepts: Does not answer with visualization bindings or encode_point_color

cases.prompt: I have a pandas DataFrame with columns 'source', 'target', and 'weight'. How do I turn that into an interactive graph visualization?

rubric: Gives the core DataFrame-to-plot workflow
Uses .edges(df, 'source', 'target') binding
Calls .plot()
oracle.reference_answer: Shows graphistry.register() plus .edges(df,'source','target') and .plot().

cases.prompt: How do I write a GFQL query to find all 3-hop paths from fraud nodes to account nodes in my graph?

rubric: Gives a GFQL query rather than deferring elsewhere
Shows e_forward() or Cypher MATCH with variable-length path
Uses g.gfql()
oracle.reference_answer: Shows chain-list or Cypher syntax for a 3-hop traversal via g.gfql().

cases.prompt: I want to run UMAP on my graph nodes using their feature columns and then visualize the clusters

rubric: Shows the UMAP workflow over node feature columns via g.umap(...)
Either g.umap(X=[...]) directly (umap auto-featurizes) or an explicit g.featurize(...).umap()
Visualizes the resulting clusters
oracle.reference_answer: g.umap(X=[feature columns]).plot(); featurize() is optional because umap() auto-featurizes given column names.

cases.prompt: I need to call the Graphistry Hub REST API with a Bearer token to download graph metadata. What's the endpoint?

rubric: Gives the REST endpoint and auth pattern
oracle.reference_answer: Gives the /api/v2/ endpoint and the Bearer-token auth pattern for downloading graph metadata.
forbidden_concepts: Does not suggest graphistry.register() Python SDK for the REST download
